sentences.text:
Brajesh Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26
February, 2021

Bench: Rajeev Kumar Shrivastava
 1 Mcrc-10074-2021
 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Mcrc-10074-2021
 (Brajesh Rathore Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
Gwalior, Dated : 26-02-2021
Shri Arshad Ali, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Smt. Abha Mishra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State.
This petition under Section 482 of CrPC has been filed for modification in Condition No. 7 of Bail order dated 22/10/2019 passed in MCRC No. 43317/2019.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that by order dated 22/10/2019 passed in MCRC No. 43317/2019, the petitioner was granted regular bail under Section 439 of CrPC under certain conditions in which condition No. 7 was that "applicant shall mark his presence before concerned trial court once every Fortnight till conclusion of trial.".

It is further submitted that the petitioner is regularly appearing before the trial Court but since petitioner is a businessman,
therefore, ofttently he has to go out from his native place and, therefore, he is facing difficulty in appearing before the trial Court in every 15 days.
Hence, prayed for exemption from compliance of condition No. 7 or modification to the same.
Per contra, learned State counsel has opposed the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner and prayed to reject the petition.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the materials available on record.
The offence against the petitioner is registered under Sections 420, 272, 273 and 120(B) of the IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of Food Safety & Standards Act.
Considering the nature of offence, this Court is not inclined to modify Condition No. 7 of bail order dated 22/10/2019 passed in MCRC No. 43317/2019.
Accordingly, this petition is hereby rejected.

ALOK KUMAR (RAJEEV KUMAR SHRIVASTAVA)
